inputs.original_text: In Palakkad on March 28, Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan rejected allegations of Rs 700 crore corruption over the Cooperative Department’s proposed common software project, describing them as political. Whatever the political framing, public money and systems serving cooperative members deserve transparent scrutiny—not just competing accusations that leave ordinary people with no clear answers.
inputs.modified_text: In Palakkad on March 28, Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan called allegations of Rs 700 crore corruption over the proposed Cooperative Department software project “political.” But calling scrutiny political doesn’t answer the public’s questions. Cooperative members and ordinary people deserve transparency over how their money and essential systems are managed, regardless of who is making the accusations. That means clear disclosure and accountability, not a political contest that leaves the people most affected in the dark.
